sections.brief: GDP per person 1980–2025 in constant 2015 dollars and PPP (World Bank WDI, Oct 2026): Israel 59.8% of the US level in 1980, 62.7% in 2025; growth per person by decade; population growth 2.2% vs 0.9% a year, total real GDP ×6.0 vs ×3.3; war years 2023–25 flat in Israel; trade openness (Israel 80% of GDP 1980 → 53% 2025; US 20% → 25%); what averages do not show. Figures: compare; stats

Israel 1984 crisis (inflation 373% annual average, 445% Dec–Dec; deficit ~14–17% of GDP; debt ~163%) and the 1 July 1985 Economic Stabilization Plan (cuts, 20% devaluation, Histadrut wage pact, price freeze, no-printing rule, $1.5bn US grant); US 1979–86 (Volcker 6 Oct 1979, funds rate 20%, unemployment 10.8%, top tax rate 70% → 50% → 28%); central banks then and now (Fed dual mandate; Bank of Israel Law 2010, 1–3% target; rates as of Sept 2026: Fed raised to 3.75–4%, BoI cut to 3.25%). Figures: time; compare

Taxes (OECD tax-to-GDP: Israel 34.0% 2000, 32.8% 2022, 29.8% 2023; US 23.6% 1965, 27.7% 2022; Israel's structure: VAT and property heavy, social security light; top rates 50% vs 37%); who pays (CBO 2022: top 1% pays 27% of federal taxes, up from 14% in 1979; Israel: about half of potential taxpayers below the income tax threshold, 2021); debt (US held by public 26% 1980 → 99% 2025 → 120% 2036; Israel ~163% mid-1980s → 132% 1990 → 77.5% 2000 → 61.9% 2023 → 68.5% 2025); deficits and interest. Figures: compare; stats

Israel's business groups (BoI 2010: ten groups controlled 41% of listed market value), the 2010–12 committee and the December 2013 Concentration Law (two-tier pyramids, financial/real separation), Delek's Phoenix sale 2018–19; US concentration (Grullon et al. 75% of industries since late 1990s vs ITIF's critique), Google search case and Sept 2025 remedy; trade (1985 FTA, 2025 goods trade, 17% → 15% tariff, Supreme Court IEEPA ruling 20 Feb 2026).
